### What does this PR do?

Updates [`docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm`](docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm) for the current Primus ROCm training image and refreshes [`docker/rocm/README.md`](docker/rocm/README.md) so the documented build matches that recipe. This follows the ROCm Dockerfile/README added in #6619.

The image now starts from `rocm/primus:v26.8` (ROCm 7.16, PyTorch 2.14) instead of the previous Primus v26.4 stack. It builds vLLM `v0.29.0` and the pinned SGLang commit, installs Ray `>=2.58.0`, and adds the Qwen3.5 Megatron extras (Gated Delta Net / `flash-linear-attention`, Megatron-Bridge on the nightly path, ISEEKYAN `mbridge` on the release path).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+rocm+dockerfile
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test

This area is not covered by CI hardware (AMD GPUs), so validation is a local image build, same as #6619.

Built `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm` and started the image on an 8× MI350X host with `/dev/kfd` and `/dev/dri` mounted. The image Python reports `torch 2.14.0+rocm10.1` and `torch.cuda.device_count() == 8`.

```sh
docker build \
    -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm \
    -t verl-rocm:local .
```

### API and Usage Example

Build args are overridable. Defaults are the Primus v26.8 / vLLM v0.29.0 recipe.

| Build arg | Default | Purpose |
| --------- | ------- | ------- |
| `PRIMUS_TAG` | `v26.8` | Base image tag. `v26.7` and `v26.8` are supported. |
| `GPU_ARCH` | `gfx942;gfx950` | `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` and `AMDGPU_TARGETS`. |
| `VERL_SOURCE` | `nightly` | `nightly` clones upstream `main` and installs Megatron-Bridge. `release` clones `VERL_REPO` / `VERL_BRANCH` and installs ISEEKYAN `mbridge`. |
| `VLLM_TAG` | `v0.29.0` | vLLM tag built from source. |
| `SGLANG_TAG` | `0801cc05ed202544e2e5c67d6b0a1d454de54fca` | SGLang commit. Re-validate when changing `PRIMUS_TAG` or `VLLM_TAG`. |
| `RAY_SPEC` | `ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0` | Ray install when `RAY_SOURCE=stable`. |
| `MAX_JOBS` | `64` | Parallel jobs for the vLLM build. |

The image runs as the non-root `verl` user and its entrypoint is `/bin/bash`, so `docker run` with no command already opens a shell. Pass the host `video` and `render` group ids so that user can open the ROCm device nodes.

```sh
docker build \
    -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm \
    --build-arg VERL_SOURCE=release \
    --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx942 \
    --build-arg MAX_JOBS=64 \
    -t verl-rocm:mi300 .
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Base image is `rocm/primus:v26.8`. PyTorch, Triton, Transformer Engine, and aiter stay on the Primus builds.
- Install `amdsmi` from the ROCm SDK tree (v26.8 via a `.pth` file, v26.7 via `pip`) and preload `rocm_sdk` with `RTLD_LOCAL`, so Ray's AMD GPU detector does not report 0 GPUs and `torch.cuda.device_count()` stays correct.
- Build vLLM `v0.29.0` from source and link `libz3.so.4.15` for tilelang. Install Ray `>=2.58.0`.
- Install verl with `--no-deps`. `VERL_SOURCE=nightly` uses upstream `main`, Megatron-Bridge `0.6.2`, and `megatron-core==0.19.2`. `VERL_SOURCE=release` uses `AMD-Ecosystem/verl` `release/0.9.0.amd0`, ISEEKYAN `mbridge`, and `megatron-core==0.18.0`.
- Add the Qwen3.5 extras: `flash-linear-attention`, `transformers>=5.12`, `mistral-common`, `mathruler`, `transferqueue`, `model-hosting-container-standards`, CuPy, and `torchao>=0.16.0`.
- Build SGLang beside vLLM (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, Triton attention). On Primus v26.8 the SGLang HIP files are compiled as C++20.
- Apply the OpenSSL and Python package security updates, drop nested Dockerfiles and VCS metadata, and run as `USER verl`.
- Rewrite `docker/rocm/README.md` for this recipe. The previous README described the Primus v26.4 / BuildKit-cache-mount build, which this Dockerfile no longer uses.

### Checklist Before Submitting

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` (Dockerfile and Markdown only; please run before merge.)
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). (`docker/rocm/README.md`.)
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: building and running this image requires AMD ROCm GPUs that CI does not provide.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`.

**Keep `docker run ` working. Use `CMD` for the default command.** `ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]` makes Bash the fixed executable. Docker passes any command arguments to Bash, so `docker run verl-rocm python train.py` runs `/bin/bash python train.py`. The documented launch in `docs/start/install.rst` ends with `verl-rocm /bin/bash`. With this entrypoint, that becomes `/bin/bash /bin/bash`, and Bash fails when it tries to run `/bin/bash` as a script. Kubernetes `args` overrides behave the same way. To clear the inherited entrypoint and keep normal command semantics, set the default command with `CMD` instead:

@@ -1,142 +1,343 @@
-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
-
-FROM pytorch_base AS install_vllm
-ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
-ENV PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"
-# Set the working dir explicitly so later RUN steps don't rely on the base
-# image's inherited WORKDIR being /workspace.
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \

+vt = Path(pip.__file__).resolve().parent / '_vendor' / 'vendor.txt'; \
+vt.write_text(vt.read_text().replace('urllib3==2.7.0', f'urllib3=={urllib3.__version__}')); \

+# Keep runtime sources under /workspace/{vllm,sglang,verl}; remove nested
+# Dockerfiles, k8s/helm manifests, docs/examples, and leftover VCS metadata.
+# Packages themselves are non-editable installs into site-packages.
+RUN rm -rf \
+        /workspace/vllm/.git \
+        /workspace/vllm/docker \
+        /workspace/vllm/docs \
+        /workspace/vllm/examples \
+        /workspace/vllm/.deps \
+        /workspace/sglang/.git \
+        /workspace/sglang/docker \
+        /workspace/sglang/.devcontainer \
+        /workspace/sglang/docs \
+        /workspace/sglang/examples \
+        /workspace/sglang/experimental \
+        /workspace/sglang/sgl-model-gateway/e2e_test \
+        /workspace/sglang/sgl-kernel/Dockerfile \
+        /workspace/verl/.git \
+        /workspace/verl/docker \
+        /workspace/.manifest/Dockerfile \
+    && find /workspace -type d -name .git -prune -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache/pip \
+    && find /tmp -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
 
+# DS-0002: run as non-root. video/render for ROCm device node access when
+# devices are group-owned; escalate at runtime if your cluster requires root.
+RUN if ! id -u verl >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
+      useradd --create-home --uid 1000 --shell /bin/bash verl \
+        || useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash verl; \
+    fi \
+    && usermod -aG video,render verl 2>/dev/null || true \
+    && chown -R verl:verl /workspace
+# aiter imports a JIT extension from outside site-packages only when
+# AITER_JIT_DIR is set. The package jit directory stays root-owned, so set
+# that variable from the current user's home on every Python startup. A fixed
+# /home/verl path would fail for any other uid. Fall back to /tmp when ~ is
+# not writable.
+# Keep this as python3 -c. A shell heredoc is not a Dockerfile heredoc on the
+# legacy builder, so a following "from pathlib" line is parsed as FROM.
+RUN python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import site; line = ("import os; os.environ.setdefault(\"AITER_JIT_DIR\", os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(\"~\"), \".aiter\", \"jit\") if os.access(os.path.expanduser(\"~\"), os.W_OK) else f\"/tmp/aiter-jit-{os.getuid()}\")\n"); path = Path(site.getsitepackages()[0]) / "aiter-jit-dir.pth"; path.write_text(line); print("wrote", path)'
+USER verl
+WORKDIR /workspace
 
-CMD ["/usr/bin/bash"]
+# Override any base-image entrypoint for interactive/training use
+ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]

@@ -1,142 +1,343 @@
-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
-
-FROM pytorch_base AS install_vllm

+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig
+
+# ── verl ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 WORKDIR /workspace

-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base

-FROM pytorch_base AS install_vllm
-ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv

-# Set the working dir explicitly so later RUN steps don't rely on the base
-# image's inherited WORKDIR being /workspace.
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig
+
+# ── verl ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 WORKDIR /workspace

+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig
+
+# ── verl ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@@ -1,142 +1,343 @@
-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
-
-FROM pytorch_base AS install_vllm
-ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
-ENV PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"
-# Set the working dir explicitly so later RUN steps don't rely on the base
-# image's inherited WORKDIR being /workspace.
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Updates [`docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm`](docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm) for the current Primus ROCm training image and refreshes [`docker/rocm/README.md`](docker/rocm/README.md) so the documented build matches that recipe. This follows the ROCm Dockerfile/README added in #6619.

The image now starts from `rocm/primus:v26.8` (ROCm 7.16, PyTorch 2.14) instead of the previous Primus v26.4 stack. It builds vLLM `v0.29.0` and the pinned SGLang commit, installs Ray `>=2.58.0`, and adds the Qwen3.5 Megatron extras (Gated Delta Net / `flash-linear-attention`, Megatron-Bridge on the nightly path, ISEEKYAN `mbridge` on the release path).

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+rocm+dockerfile
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test

This area is not covered by CI hardware (AMD GPUs), so validation is a local image build, same as #6619.

Built `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm` and started the image on an 8× MI350X host with `/dev/kfd` and `/dev/dri` mounted. The image Python reports `torch 2.14.0+rocm10.1` and `torch.cuda.device_count() == 8`.

```sh
docker build \
    -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm \
    -t verl-rocm:local .
```

### API and Usage Example

Build args are overridable. Defaults are the Primus v26.8 / vLLM v0.29.0 recipe.

| Build arg | Default | Purpose |
| --------- | ------- | ------- |
| `PRIMUS_TAG` | `v26.8` | Base image tag. `v26.7` and `v26.8` are supported. |
| `GPU_ARCH` | `gfx942;gfx950` | `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` and `AMDGPU_TARGETS`. |
| `VERL_SOURCE` | `nightly` | `nightly` clones upstream `main` and installs Megatron-Bridge. `release` clones `VERL_REPO` / `VERL_BRANCH` and installs ISEEKYAN `mbridge`. |
| `VLLM_TAG` | `v0.29.0` | vLLM tag built from source. |
| `SGLANG_TAG` | `0801cc05ed202544e2e5c67d6b0a1d454de54fca` | SGLang commit. Re-validate when changing `PRIMUS_TAG` or `VLLM_TAG`. |
| `RAY_SPEC` | `ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0` | Ray install when `RAY_SOURCE=stable`. |
| `MAX_JOBS` | `64` | Parallel jobs for the vLLM build. |

The image runs as the non-root `verl` user and its entrypoint is `/bin/bash`, so `docker run` with no command already opens a shell. Pass the host `video` and `render` group ids so that user can open the ROCm device nodes.

```sh
docker build \
    -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm \
    --build-arg VERL_SOURCE=release \
    --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx942 \
    --build-arg MAX_JOBS=64 \
    -t verl-rocm:mi300 .
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Base image is `rocm/primus:v26.8`. PyTorch, Triton, Transformer Engine, and aiter stay on the Primus builds.
- Install `amdsmi` from the ROCm SDK tree (v26.8 via a `.pth` file, v26.7 via `pip`) and preload `rocm_sdk` with `RTLD_LOCAL`, so Ray's AMD GPU detector does not report 0 GPUs and `torch.cuda.device_count()` stays correct.
- Build vLLM `v0.29.0` from source and link `libz3.so.4.15` for tilelang. Install Ray `>=2.58.0`.
- Install verl with `--no-deps`. `VERL_SOURCE=nightly` uses upstream `main`, Megatron-Bridge `0.6.2`, and `megatron-core==0.19.2`. `VERL_SOURCE=release` uses `AMD-Ecosystem/verl` `release/0.9.0.amd0`, ISEEKYAN `mbridge`, and `megatron-core==0.18.0`.
- Add the Qwen3.5 extras: `flash-linear-attention`, `transformers>=5.12`, `mistral-common`, `mathruler`, `transferqueue`, `model-hosting-container-standards`, CuPy, and `torchao>=0.16.0`.
- Build SGLang beside vLLM (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, Triton attention). On Primus v26.8 the SGLang HIP files are compiled as C++20.
- Apply the OpenSSL and Python package security updates, drop nested Dockerfiles and VCS metadata, and run as `USER verl`.
- Rewrite `docker/rocm/README.md` for this recipe. The previous README described the Primus v26.4 / BuildKit-cache-mount build, which this Dockerfile no longer uses.

### Checklist Before Submitting

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` (Dockerfile and Markdown only; please run before merge.)
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). (`docker/rocm/README.md`.)
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: building and running this image requires AMD ROCm GPUs that CI does not provide.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`.

files.patch:
@@ -1,142 +1,345 @@
-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
-
-FROM pytorch_base AS install_vllm
-ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
-ENV PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"
-# Set the working dir explicitly so later RUN steps don't rely on the base
-# image's inherited WORKDIR being /workspace.
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig
+
+# ── verl ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 WORKDIR /workspace
-ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
-
-# Install Causal-Conv1d and its dependencies
-ARG CAUSAL_CONV1D_REPO=https://github.com/Dao-AILab/causal-conv1d
-ARG CAUSAL_CONV1D_BRANCH=e940ead2fd962c56854455017541384909ca669f
-
-ENV CAUSAL_CONV1D_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE
-ENV MAMBA_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE
-ENV HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx942,gfx950
-
-RUN cd /workspace \
-    && git clone ${CAUSAL_CONV1D_REPO} causal-conv1d \
-    && cd causal-conv1d \
-    && git checkout ${CAUSAL_CONV1D_BRANCH} \
-    && git show --oneline -s \
-    && pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation . \
-    && cd .. \
-    && rm -fr causal-conv1d
-
-ARG VLLM_TAG="18d87a87dc39c1a50f452b218fdcc3aeec48d18e"
-RUN pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm && \
-    cd /workspace && git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm && \
-    cd vllm && git checkout ${VLLM_TAG} && \
-    # [V1] Add sleep/wake correctness regression test for hybrid GDN
-    # Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44972
-    sed -i 's|\(  // std::cout << "create_and_map:\)|#ifdef USE_ROCM\n  // ROCm: zero freshly mapped VRAM to avoid stale data (PR #44972)\n  CUDA_CHECK((CUresult)hipMemset(reinterpret_cast<void*>(d_mem), 0, size));\n  if (error_code != 0) {\n    return;\n  }\n#endif\n\1|' csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp && \
-    # [Bugfix][MoE] Preserve unquantized weight storage on ROCm
-    # Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46009
-    sed -i 's/layer\.w13_weight\.data = self\._maybe_pad_weight(layer\.w13_weight\.data)/layer.w13_weight.data.copy_(self._maybe_pad_weight(layer.w13_weight.data))/' \
-      /workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/unquantized_fused_moe_method.py && \
-    sed -i 's/layer\.w2_weight\.data = self\._maybe_pad_weight(layer\.w2_weight\.data)/layer.w2_weight.data.copy_(self._maybe_pad_weight(layer.w2_weight.data))/' \
-      /workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/unquantized_fused_moe_method.py && \
-    sed -i 's/return w13_weight\.contiguous(), w2_weight\.contiguous()/return w13_weight, w2_weight/' \
-      /workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/unquantized.py && \
-    pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt && \
-    MAX_JOBS=64 python3 setup.py develop --no-deps
-RUN pip uninstall tilelang -y && pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps xgrammar==0.1.32
-
-
-FROM install_vllm AS install_verl
-ARG VERL_TAG="7b19203c52503760f92e0368067c7eb744236274"
-RUN cd /workspace && git clone https://github.com/verl-project/verl.git && \
-    cd verl && git checkout ${VERL_TAG} && \
-    git submodule update --init --recursive && \
-    sed -i 's/^  vllm: {}/  vllm:\n    disable_custom_all_reduce: True/' /workspace/verl/verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml && \
-    sed -i 's/^  sglang: {}/  sglang:\n    disable_custom_all_reduce: True\n    attention_backend: triton/' /workspace/verl/verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml && \
-    pip install --no-cache-dir . 
-    
-# for qwen3.5 — versions pinned to what was validated on this image for reproducibility.
-RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
-    "git+https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/mbridge.git@a61943d7fcb34a190471cfeb0a0eb8bbda621ddf" \
-    mcore_bridge==1.5.2 \
-    megatron-core==0.18.0 \
-    mathruler==0.1.0 \
-    qwen_vl_utils==0.0.14 \
-    datasets==5.0.0 \
-    accelerate==1.14.0 \
-    TransferQueue==0.1.11 \
-    flash-linear-attention==0.5.1
+RUN if [ "$VERL_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \

+that becomes an argument to the entrypoint, and Bash then fails with
+`cannot execute binary file`. Pass the host `video` and `render` group ids

+From: Tiffany Mintz <Tiffany.Mintz@amd.com>

+Subject: [PATCH] [Fix] [AMD] layernorm: call vLLM fused_add_rms_norm in place
+
+On ROCm without aiter, RMSNorm.forward_hip and GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip
+bound fused_add_rms_norm from vLLM and called it with six arguments.
+vLLM's op is the four-argument in-place API, so the first residual
+layer raised TypeError. Call it in place, and skip the HIP kernels for
+an empty batch because they fail to launch.

+ python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py         | 29 ++++---
+ .../unit/layers/test_layernorm_hip_vllm.py    | 85 +++++++++++++++++++
+ 2 files changed, 100 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
+ create mode 100644 test/registered/unit/layers/test_layernorm_hip_vllm.py
+

++            # vLLM's HIP kernels fail to launch on an empty grid.

++"""On ROCm without aiter, RMSNorm and GemmaRMSNorm with a residual must call vLLM's
++fused_add_rms_norm with its in-place (input, residual, weight, epsilon) signature
++and match forward_native."""
++
++import unittest
++from unittest.mock import patch
++
++import torch
++
++from sglang.srt.layers import layernorm
++from sglang.srt.layers.layernorm import GemmaRMSNorm, RMSNorm
++from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
++from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
++
++register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
++
++HIDDEN = 64
++
++
++def _vllm_fused_add_rms_norm(
++    input: torch.Tensor, residual: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, epsilon: float
++) -> None:
++    # Reference for vllm._custom_ops.fused_add_rms_norm: residual += input, then
++    # input = rms_norm(residual) * weight, both in place.
++    residual.add_(input)
++    r = residual.float()
++    normed = r * torch.rsqrt(r.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + epsilon)
++    input.copy_((normed * weight.float()).to(input.dtype))
++
++
++def _vllm_rms_norm(
++    out: torch.Tensor, input: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, epsilon: float
++) -> None:
++    x = input.float()
++    normed = x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + epsilon)
++    out.copy_((normed * weight.float()).to(out.dtype))
++
++
++class TestLayerNormHipVllm(CustomTestCase):
++    def setUp(self):
++        self.patches = [
++            patch.object(layernorm, "_use_aiter", False),
++            patch.object(layernorm, "_has_vllm_rms_norm", True),
++            patch.object(
++                layernorm, "fused_add_rms_norm", _vllm_fused_add_rms_norm, create=True
++            ),
++            patch.object(layernorm, "rms_norm", _vllm_rms_norm, create=True),
++        ]
++        for p in self.patches:
++            p.start()
++        torch.manual_seed(0)
++
++    def tearDown(self):
++        for p in reversed(self.patches):
++            p.stop()
++
++    def _check(self, layer, num_tokens, post):
++        x = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN)
++        residual = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN)
++        post_add = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN) if post else None
++        ref_out, ref_residual = layer.forward_native(
++            x.clone(), residual.clone(), None if post_add is None else post_add.clone()
++        )
++        out, out_residual = layer.forward_hip(x.clone(), residual.clone(), post_add)
++        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref_out)
++        torch.testing.assert_close(out_residual, ref_residual)
++
++    def test_rms_norm_with_residual(self):
++        layer = RMSNorm(HIDDEN, eps=1e-6)
++        with torch.no_grad():
++            layer.weight.normal_(mean=1.0, std=0.1)
++        for num_tokens in (0, 7):
++            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens):
++                self._check(layer, num_tokens=num_tokens, post=False)

++    def test_gemma_rms_norm_with_residual(self):
++        layer = GemmaRMSNorm(HIDDEN, eps=1e-6)

++            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens, post=post):
++                self._check(layer, num_tokens=num_tokens, post=post)
++
++
++if __name__ == "__main__":
++    unittest.main()

**Keep `docker run ` working. Use `CMD` for the default command.** `ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]` makes Bash the fixed executable. Docker passes any command arguments to Bash, so `docker run verl-rocm python train.py` runs `/bin/bash python train.py`. The documented launch in `docs/start/install.rst` ends with `verl-rocm /bin/bash`. With this entrypoint, that becomes `/bin/bash /bin/bash`, and Bash fails when it tries to run `/bin/bash` as a script. Kubernetes `args` overrides behave the same way. +# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"

+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net

+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \

+    && ldconfig

+    && sed -i 's|f"--amdgpu-target={amdgpu_target}"|"--offload-arch=gfx942", "--offload-arch=gfx950"|' setup_rocm.py \
+    && sed -i '/amdgpu_target not in \["gfx942", "gfx950"\]/,/sys.exit(1)/d' setup_rocm.py \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/' setup_rocm.py; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -zi 's/#if HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ\n#include <c10\/util\/Float8_e4m3fnuz.h>\nusing FP8_TYPE = c10::Float8_e4m3fnuz;\nconstexpr auto FP8_E4M3_MAX = 224.0f;\n#else\n#if HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3\n#include <c10\/util\/Float8_e4m3fn.h>\nusing FP8_TYPE = c10::Float8_e4m3fn;\nC10_HOST_DEVICE constexpr auto FP8_E4M3_MAX = std::numeric_limits<FP8_TYPE>::max();\n#else\n#error "fp8 is not supported in this processor (arch < gfx942)."\n#endif  \/\/ HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3\n#endif  \/\/ HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ/#if defined(__gfx942__)\n#include <c10\/util\/Float8_e4m3fnuz.h>\nusing FP8_TYPE = c10::Float8_e4m3fnuz;\nconstexpr auto FP8_E4M3_MAX = 224.0f;\n#else\n#include <c10\/util\/Float8_e4m3fn.h>\nusing FP8_TYPE = c10::Float8_e4m3fn;\nC10_HOST_DEVICE constexpr auto FP8_E4M3_MAX = std::numeric_limits<FP8_TYPE>::max();\n#endif  \/\/ __gfx942__/' include/utils.h \

+    && apt-get update \

+        libssl3t64 \
+        linux-libc-dev \

-ARG GIT_COMMIT_TAG=DEV

+# _vendor; pip may still vendor urllib3 2.7.0.
+RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -U 'pip>=26' 'setuptools>=80' \
+    && SITE="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+    && rm -rf \
+        ${SITE}/setuptools/_vendor/jaraco.context-*.dist-info \
+        ${SITE}/setuptools/_vendor/jaraco/context \
+        ${SITE}/setuptools/_vendor/jaraco/context.py \
+        ${SITE}/setuptools/_vendor/wheel-*.dist-info \
+        ${SITE}/setuptools/_vendor/wheel \
+    && python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; import shutil, pip, urllib3; \
+vendor = Path(pip.__file__).resolve().parent / '_vendor' / 'urllib3'; \
+src = Path(urllib3.__file__).resolve().parent; \
+vendor.exists() and shutil.rmtree(vendor); \
+shutil.copytree(src, vendor); \
+vt = Path(pip.__file__).resolve().parent / '_vendor' / 'vendor.txt'; \
+vt.write_text(vt.read_text().replace('urllib3==2.7.0', f'urllib3=={urllib3.__version__}')); \

+# Keep runtime sources under /workspace/{vllm,sglang,verl}; remove nested
+# Dockerfiles, k8s/helm manifests, docs/examples, and leftover VCS metadata.
+# Packages themselves are non-editable installs into site-packages.
+RUN rm -rf \

+        /workspace/vllm/docker \
+        /workspace/vllm/docs \
+        /workspace/vllm/examples \

+        /workspace/sglang/.git \
+        /workspace/sglang/docker \

+        /workspace/verl/.git \
+        /workspace/verl/docker \

+# DS-0002: run as non-root. video/render for ROCm device node access when
+# devices are group-owned; escalate at runtime if your cluster requires root.
+RUN if ! id -u verl >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
+      useradd --create-home --uid 1000 --shell /bin/bash verl \
+        || useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash verl; \
+    fi \
+    && usermod -aG video,render verl 2>/dev/null || true \
+    && chown -R verl:verl /workspace
+# aiter imports a JIT extension from outside site-packages only when
+# AITER_JIT_DIR is set. The package jit directory stays root-owned, so set
+# that variable from the current user's home on every Python startup. A fixed
+# /home/verl path would fail for any other uid. Fall back to /tmp when ~ is
+# not writable.
+# Keep this as python3 -c. A shell heredoc is not a Dockerfile heredoc on the
+# legacy builder, so a following "from pathlib" line is parsed as FROM.
+RUN python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import site; line = ("import os; os.environ.setdefault(\"AITER_JIT_DIR\", os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(\"~\"), \".aiter\", \"jit\") if os.access(os.path.expanduser(\"~\"), os.W_OK) else f\"/tmp/aiter-jit-{os.getuid()}\")\n"); path = Path(site.getsitepackages()[0]) / "aiter-jit-dir.pth"; path.write_text(line); print("wrote", path)'
+USER verl
+WORKDIR /workspace
 
-CMD ["/usr/bin/bash"]
+# Override any base-image entrypoint for interactive/training use
+ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]

+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=rocm/primus
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+FROM ${PRIMUS_REPO}:${PRIMUS_TAG}
+
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-ceuxo", "pipefail"]
+
+# gfx942 = MI300X, gfx950 = MI350X
+ARG GPU_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+
+ARG VERL_SOURCE="nightly" # "release" or "nightly"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="release/0.9.0.amd0"
+
+
+ARG RAY_SPEC="ray[default,serve]>=2.58.0"
+ARG RAY_SOURCE="stable"
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+
+# ── Runtime environment variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus:v26.4 already ships torch and TransformerEngine (ROCm 7.14 /
+# torch 2.12 / TE 2.14.dev0, matching README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md's tested
+# environment), but it is a *training-only* image: it does not ship vllm
+# (built from source below) or megatron-core (installed with the Qwen3.5
+# extras below). So this Dockerfile layers those, verl itself, and the
+# Qwen3.5 extras documented in that README's "Install dependencies" section.
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV AMDGPU_TARGETS="${GPU_ARCH}"
+ENV VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm
+
+# vLLM ROCm performance flags (see README_qwen3_5_35b_rocm.md "ROCm-specific
+# configuration notes"); run_qwen3_5_35b_megatron.sh re-exports the AITER ones
+# with its own defaults, so these just fix the image-level defaults.
+ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_ACT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_WEIGHT_PADDING=1
+ENV VLLM_FP8_REDUCE_CONV=1
+ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+
+# RCCL tuning (can be overridden at runtime for multi-node)
+ENV NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+
+# ── amdsmi (AMD SMI Python bindings) ──────────────────────────────────────────
+# This image's ROCm is the pip-installed TheRock SDK (_rocm_sdk_core /
+# _rocm_sdk_devel), which bundles the amd_smi library/CLI but not the `amdsmi`
+# Python package itself (open upstream gap: github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/3054).
+# Without it, `import amdsmi` fails, and Ray's AMD GPU accelerator manager
+# (ray._private.thirdparty.pyamdsmi) silently catches that ImportError and
+# reports 0 GPUs, so verl's resource-pool check fails with
+# "Total available GPUs 0 is less than total desired GPUs 8" even though
+# torch/rocm-smi see all GPUs fine.
+#
+# v26.7 ships a pip-installable source tree at share/amd_smi.
+# v26.8 ships the installed package at share/amd_smi/amdsmi and loads
+# libamd_smi.so.27 from <sdk>/lib by a path relative to that file, so the
+# package has to stay in place. A site-packages .pth adds it to sys.path.
+#
+# Loading amdsmi introduces a duplicate `libamd_smi` ODR clash with
+# rocm_sdk's RTLD_GLOBAL library preloading, which breaks
+# torch.cuda.device_count() (returns 0 despite cuda.is_available()==True).
+# The workaround (from the same upstream issue thread) is to make rocm_sdk
+# preload libraries with RTLD_LOCAL instead of RTLD_GLOBAL.
+ARG PRIMUS_TAG=v26.8
+ENV PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG}
+RUN ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import _rocm_sdk_core, os; print(os.path.dirname(_rocm_sdk_core.__file__))')" \
+    && if [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.7" ]; then \
+         pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi"; \
+       elif [ "$PRIMUS_TAG" = "v26.8" ]; then \
+         SITE_PACKAGES="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])')" \
+         && printf '%s\n' "${ROCM_SDK_CORE_DIR}/share/amd_smi" > "${SITE_PACKAGES}/amdsmi.pth"; \
+       else \
+         echo "Unsupported PRIMUS_TAG=${PRIMUS_TAG} for the amdsmi install" >&2; \
+         exit 1; \
+       fi \
+    && sed -i 's/rtld_global: bool = True/rtld_global: bool = False/g' \
+        "$(python3 -c 'import rocm_sdk, os; print(os.path.dirname(rocm_sdk.__file__))')/__init__.py"
+
+# ── Ray ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+RUN PY_TAG="cp$(echo ${PYTHON_VERSION} | tr -d '.')" && \
+    if [ "$RAY_SOURCE" = "nightly" ]; then \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true && \
+      pip install -U \
+        "ray[default,serve] @ https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ray-wheels/latest/ray-3.0.0.dev0-${PY_TAG}-${PY_TAG}-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl"; \
+    else \
+      pip uninstall -y ray 2>/dev/null || true \
+      && pip install --no-cache-dir "${RAY_SPEC}"; \
+    fi
+
+# ── vLLM (ROCm, from source) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# rocm/primus is a training-only image (Megatron-LM / TorchTitan backends) and
+# does not ship vllm at all, so verl's vllm rollout backend fails to import
+# with "vllm version None not supported" unless it's built here. Unlike
+# Dockerfile.old's vllm-dev *build-only* base image, rocm/primus already
+# exposes a working ROCM_PATH/HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH pointing at its pip-installed
+# _rocm_sdk_devel (via the /opt/rocm symlink), so no per-RUN path overrides
+# are needed here -- just CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (unset by default) and the
+# libamdhip64 symlink some of vLLM's build tooling expects under /usr/lib.
+# Built from VLLM_TAG, not main HEAD. The default is v0.29.0, matching the
+# vllm==0.29.0 pin in verl-project/verl main's vllm extra.
+ARG VLLM_REPO=https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
+ARG VLLM_TAG=v0.29.0
+ARG MAX_JOBS=64
+ENV MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS}
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm \
+    && cd /workspace/vllm \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir setuptools_scm \
+    && ln -sf ${ROCM_PATH}/lib/libamdhip64.so /usr/lib/libamdhip64.so \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements/rocm.txt \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${ROCM_PATH}/lib/cmake \
+       pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
+    && pip install --no-cache-dir gguf \
+    # Drop Rust tree after build: Cargo.lock is not needed at runtime and the
+    # compiled extensions are already installed into site-packages.
+    && rm -rf /workspace/vllm/rust
+
+# ── libz3 (fix tilelang/tvm dlopen failure) ──────────────────────────────────
+# vLLM's requirements/rocm.txt pulls in tilelang (via amd-quark), which
+# bundles a prebuilt libtvm_compiler.so that hard-requires the exact soname
+# libz3.so.4.15. The z3-solver pip wheel *does* ship that exact file, but
+# only inside its own egg dir (not on the linker search path or in the
+# ldconfig cache), and the apt-installed libz3-4 only provides libz3.so.4
+# (no .15 suffix) which doesn't satisfy the NEEDED entry. Without this,
+# `import tilelang` (pulled in transitively by megatron-core's GatedDeltaNet
+# -> fla -> mamba_ssm -> tilelang, needed for Qwen3.5's Gated Delta Net
+# linear-attention layers) fails with
+# "OSError: libz3.so.4.15: cannot open shared object file". Fix: symlink the
+# wheel's bundled .so into a system linker path and refresh ldconfig.
+RUN Z3_LIB_DIR="$(python3 -c 'import z3, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(z3.__file__), "lib"))')" \
+    && ln -sf "${Z3_LIB_DIR}/libz3.so.4.15" /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz3.so.4.15 \
+    && ldconfig
+
+# ── verl ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 WORKDIR /workspace

-ARG DEFAULT_BASE=rocm/primus:v26.4
-ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
-FROM ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
